title: POST /api/auth/forgot-password — send reset email
description: Implement the forgot password flow: accept an email, generate a short-lived reset token, store it, and send a reset email via Resend.
acceptanceCriteria: Always returns 200 (do not reveal if email exists)
If email exists, sends a password reset email with a unique link
Token is stored hashed in the database (can reuse refresh_tokens table or a separate password_reset_tokens table)

steps.details: Add a password_reset_tokens table: id (uuid pk), user_id (uuid FK → users cascade delete), token_hash (text notNull), expires_at (timestamp notNull), used_at (timestamp nullable), created_at (timestamp defaultNow()). Run db:migrate.

1) Validate email. 2) Look up user by email (soft-delete filter). 3) If not found, return 200 with generic message (no info leak). 4) Generate crypto.randomBytes(32).toString('hex') as reset token. 5) Hash with bcrypt and store in password_reset_tokens with expires_at = 1 hour from now. 6) Call email service to send reset link: FRONTEND_URL/reset-password?token=RAW_TOKEN. 7) Return 200 { message: 'If that email exists, a reset link has been sent.' }
POST /api/auth/forgot-password with a registered email — verify 200 and email is sent (check Resend dashboard or logs). POST with unknown email — verify same 200 response, no email sent.

technicalNotes: Always return 200 to prevent email enumeration
crypto.randomBytes is cryptographically secure — use it, not Math.random()
Reset tokens should be single-use: mark used_at on redemption
